I've been working this land for 35 years. I know my soil, I know this county's weather, I know what my body can still do at 63. My sons and daughter-in-law earn wages in the city, so most of the fieldwork falls to me and my husband. I need to keep things manageable.

Wheat is my foundation — it goes in every autumn and feeds us through winter and into next year. I'll put the most land to it, about 5 mu. It's reliable. I know the timing by heart.

After wheat harvest in June, I'll rotate 3 mu of that land into summer maize. Maize needs less watching than sunflower and the yield is decent. I'll buy hybrid seed from the county co-op — everyone around here does now, and the yields are clearly better. My neighbor stopped using his saved seed five years ago and I followed him.

My sunflower I'll keep to 1.5 mu — that's my cash. Sunflower oil sells well locally. But sunflower is harder work at harvest, and with fewer hands, I can't overextend. I'll use improved seed. Not hybrid — too expensive and I can't always get it on time.

For fertilizer I go by what my father-in-law taught me and what I've seen work. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and urea later for wheat and maize. I don't do soil tests — I just watch the color of the leaves. For irrigation I'll pump the well: wheat needs water at sowing, jointing, heading, and grain fill — that's 4 times if it doesn't rain. Maize I'll water 2-3 times in summer because the rains usually help. Sunflower 2-3 times.

I'll rotary till before planting — easier on my back than deep ploughing, and it's enough.
